Description:
A torus drilled through by a cylinder that runs parallel to the torus axis but through the TUBE, not
through the hole. Both bodies are built from exact NURBS circles and neither surface is a quadric of
CADability's own: the torus is a solid.sweep of a circle r = 8 along a circle R = 30 and comes out as
SweptCurveSurface, the rod is a solid.extrude of a circle r = 10 and comes out as
SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion.

  nurbsTorus  R = 30, r = 8 about the z axis
  nurbsRod    r = 10 about the vertical line through (30, 0, 0), from z = -20 to z = 40 - 20 = 20,
              so it reaches well beyond the tube, whose z never leaves [-8, 8]

The rod's axis pierces the CENTRE CIRCLE of the tube at (30, 0, 0), which is the deliberate part: the
cut is as deep as it can be without being symmetric in any useful way, and the intersection curve wraps
around the tube twice over instead of being a plane section. It is still entirely transversal - the
contact condition for these two canal surfaces asks for a common normal perpendicular to BOTH spines,
which forces the rod's spine parameter to 0 and then the two inscribed spheres are concentric with radii
8 and 10 and cannot touch. There is no tangential contact in this case.

The rod being LONGER than the tube is what makes the numbers below simple: the intersection is exactly
the part of the torus that lies inside the infinite cylinder, and neither rod cap takes part in it.
Expected:
Two closed solids and four closed results.

  nurbsTorus  V = 2*pi^2*R*r^2 = 2*pi^2*30*64 = 37899.2809001831
              A = 4*pi^2*R*r = 4*pi^2*240 = 9474.8202250458
              extent -38, -38, -8 .. 38, 38, 8, and no cap at all - the path closes
  nurbsRod    V = pi*10^2*40 = 12566.3706143592
              A = 2*pi*10*40 + 2*pi*10^2 = 3141.5926535898
              extent 20, -10, -20 .. 40, 10, 20

The one value that is not elementary is the intersection, and it was computed independently of the code
under test, as the integral of the tube's thickness over the rod's cross section:

  V = 2 * integral over theta of  integral over rho of  2*sqrt(64 - (rho-30)^2) * rho  d rho d theta

with rho between the two roots of rho^2 - 60*rho*cos(theta) + 800 = 0 clipped to [22, 38]. The inner
integral is elementary, the outer one was taken with the substitution that removes both square root
endpoints and evaluated by composite Simpson; it is stationary to twelve digits over a sixteenfold
refinement:

  torusRodInter   3673.793333506

A Monte Carlo over the rod's bounding box with 4e6 samples gives 3674.811 +- 1.582, which is 0.6 sigma
away - the two methods share nothing but the geometry.

From it everything else follows exactly:
  torusRodUnion   37899.2809001831 + 12566.3706143592 - 3673.7933335 = 46791.8581810
  torusMinusRod   37899.2809001831 - 3673.7933335 = 34225.4875667
  rodMinusTorus   12566.3706143592 - 3673.7933335 =  8892.5772809

The SHAPE of torusMinusRod is worth stating because it is the counter-intuitive one: at theta = 0 the
rod covers rho from 20 to 40 and therefore the whole cross section of the tube, so the ring is CUT
THROUGH. What is left is one open arc - a single solid of Euler 2, not a ring of Euler 0 and not two
pieces. rodMinusTorus is one solid as well: the tube only reaches |z| <= 8 while the rod runs to
|z| = 20, so material is left above and below in any case.
The remaining topology - how many faces the results are partitioned into and whether any quadric is
recognized behind the NURBS surfaces - is the implementation's choice and is pinned by the recorded
fingerprint, not by this prose.

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS - HISTORICAL, THE DEFECT IS FIXED. A planar face whose outline is a
rational NURBS circle used to be measured through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea ->
GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for most radii that biarc approximation
degenerated into four straight lines, so the lid measured 2*r*r instead of pi*r*r. It was not even a
threshold: exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5,
6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25. Every radius in this case was therefore taken from the first list, so
that its numbers would be the geometry and not a measurement artefact.
Since 2026-09-21 BSpline2D integrates the swept area of a rational spline instead of approximating it
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and every radius is exact. The radii here are left as they are -
they cost nothing and the case does not need rewriting - but a new case no longer has to avoid any.
Status:
Green from the day it was written, 2026-09-17. All four operations return and every volume meets its
reference within 1.1e-4, which for the three results is the accuracy of the measurement rather than of
the operation: volume on a curved face is summed over its triangulation, and the deviations have both
signs (the intersection and rodMinusTorus measure high, torusMinusRod low). Stable over 3 repeats.

The operand nurbsTorus matches the TorusFromNurbsSweep baseline field for field - same volume, area,
edgeLength and surface histogram - although the two cases build it through independent calls. That is
the strongest check there is that the sweep itself has not moved.

The shapes are the ones the Expected section predicts, including the one that is easy to get wrong:
torusMinusRod is ONE solid of Euler 2, because the rod covers the whole cross section of the tube at
theta = 0 and cuts the ring through, and rodMinusTorus has Euler 0, because the tube leaves a tunnel
through the rod.

nurbsRod.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 12566.3705834 against 12566.3706144, 2.5e-09. two SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion faces and two lids.

nurbsTorus.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 37899.2808124 against 37899.2809002, 2.3e-09. identical to the TorusFromNurbsSweep baseline in every field. Four SweptCurveSurface faces and no lid - the path closes.

rodMinusTorus.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 8893.5594237 against 8892.5772809, 1.1e-04. Euler 0 - the tube leaves a tunnel through the rod.

torusMinusRod.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 34224.501511 against 34225.4875667, 2.9e-05. One solid of Euler 2: the ring IS cut through at theta = 0, which is what makes this the interesting one of the two differences.

torusRodInter.verified: 2026-09-17 GH: volume 3674.16015003 against 3673.79333351, 1.0e-04. against the quadrature value given in Expected, which a Monte Carlo of 4e6 samples confirms independently at 3674.811 +- 1.582.
